chunks: Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-ʿAlaʾ ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (Imams) عليهما السلام.

key_terms.أَحَدِهِمَا: one of the two; i.e., one of the two Imams عليهما السلام
key_terms.ذَلِكَ: that; referring back to the prior hadith content
key_terms.سَعْدُ: Saʿd, the opening narrator in the chain
key_terms.مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سِنَانٍ: Muhammad ibn Sinan, a transmitter in the sanad/isnad
key_terms.مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ مُسْلِمٍ: Muhammad ibn Muslim, a major transmitter in the chain
key_terms.مِثْلَ: like; indicating sameness with a previous report

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith phrase “مِثْلَ ذَلِكَ” mean in a narrated report on funeral prayer?
ai.summary: This report gives a sanad/isnad ending with one of the two Imams عليهما السلام, then states: “the like of that,” indicating that the wording or ruling is the same as a preceding hadith. In the chapter context, it relates to the places in which salat over funerals is performed.
